title: Can a Beginner Climb Kilimanjaro?
excerpt: You do not need climbing experience for Kilimanjaro. You do need good preparation, enough days and the right attitude. Here is what beginners should know.
body:
Kilimanjaro is the highest mountain in Africa, and yet many people who climb it have never been on a mountain before. That is possible because the main routes are walking routes, not technical climbs.

## What you do not need

- Climbing experience or ropes.
- Special technical skills.
- To be an athlete.

## What you do need

- **Reasonable fitness.** You walk several days in a row, five to eight hours a day. A [12-week training plan](/blog/kilimanjaro-training-plan/) helps.
- **Time.** Seven or eight days on the mountain gives your body a better chance to adapt.
- **Patience.** Walking slowly is the most important skill.
- **The right gear.** See our [packing list](/blog/kilimanjaro-packing-list/).
- **A good crew** that checks on you every day.

## Best routes for beginners

- [Lemosho](/blog/kilimanjaro-lemosho-route-guide/), eight days: gradual and scenic.
- [Machame](/blog/kilimanjaro-machame-route-guide/), seven days: popular and well supported.
- [Rongai](/blog/kilimanjaro-rongai-route-guide/), seven days: quiet with steady gradients.

## A good first step

If you want to test yourself, a climb of [Mount Meru](/blog/mount-meru-climb-guide/) before Kilimanjaro is excellent preparation.

## Honest note

Not everyone reaches the summit, and that is fine. Many people who turn back at Stella Point or lower still call it one of the best experiences of their life.
